publicationStmt.p: Working authority file for the Digital Corpus of Armenian Colophons. Publication details and licensing will be established for the corpus.

sourceDesc.p: Witness records will be established from the project inventory, manuscript images, catalogues, and reviewed colophon texts. Each record retains supporting evidence.

projectDesc.p: A witness is a particular surviving occurrence of a colophon text. Each witness links one colophon identity to the manuscript preserving that occurrence and, where relevant, to its codicological unit. Several witnesses can point to one colophon, and several witnesses of distinct colophons can point to the same manuscript.

The colophon identity is defined in colophons.xml; the physical manuscript is defined in manuscripts.xml. Transcriptions, translations, annotations, image alignment, and comparisons are encoded in the individual colophon editions and reference these stable witness records.

editorialDecl.p: Witness identifiers follow the pattern col-000001-wit-000001. Number witnesses from 000001 within each colophon; the full identifier is unique.

Use one witness element per occurrence, inside listWit. Reserve witness/@corresp for its link to the colophon identity, such as colophons.xml#col-000001. Use ref/@type manuscript for the link to manuscripts.xml. These are project conventions to be enforced in the corpus customisation.

Where a colophon survives on a reused flyleaf or other distinct codicological unit, add a ref of type codicologicalUnit to the relevant msPart identifier. Retain the link to the host manuscript as well. Being a flyleaf alone does not establish a separate unit or determine whether the inscription is original.
Record the physical locus in locus, including folio ranges, column positions, and flyleaf designations as appropriate.

A note of type hand may link to a handNote in manuscripts.xml. Attribute a physical hand to a historical person only with supporting evidence, using persName/@ref in a separate note of type attribution. A named original scribe in a later copy is not automatically the writer of that surviving inscription.
Record completeness, condition, and unresolved identification questions as needed. Bibliographical references point to bibliography.xml.
